assumptions.anchor: local occupation median for later illustrations; TWC lower-third proxy for entry when available
assumptions.upperBound: No modeled stage above the larger of the observed median and upper-quartile wage; absent an upper quartile, no stage above 1.20 × anchor.

sources.publisher: Texas Workforce Commission / Labor Market Information
sources.title: 2025 Annual MSA Wages · Entry wage proxy
sources.role: Mean wage of the lowest-paid one-third of workers in the selected occupation and location. It is an entry wage proxy, not observed pay by years of experience.

sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via O*NET OnLine
sources.title: OEWS May 2025 · Austin metro
sources.role: Local wage anchor; all experience ratios are Fieldguide assumptions.

sources.title: How to use occupational wages
sources.role: Wage variation guidance; does not publish experience-year estimates.

notes: Mean wage of the lowest-paid one-third of workers in the selected occupation and location. It is an entry wage proxy, not observed pay by years of experience.
Starts after the required clinical education and credentials. Later figures exclude advanced-practice qualifications, overtime, and management promotions.
Figures hold purchasing power constant. No future inflation is added. Future labor-market conditions and personal outcomes can differ.
Entry means a first full-time qualified job after required preparation. Experience years begin there; education and apprenticeship years are separate.
Practice pay below starts after family medicine residency. The paid residency stage comes first. Other specialties have different routes and earnings.

nextSteps.title: Talk it through and choose a next step
nextSteps.detail: Share your notes with a counselor, teacher, or trusted adult. Ask about one class, club, or supervised activity to try next. Keep college options open while you explore. Revisit your answers after a new experience.

nextSteps.title: Build three pieces for a small portfolio
nextSteps.detail: Design a poster, a simple visual identity, and a digital layout. Ask for feedback and revise one piece. Notice whether critique and revisions hold your interest.
nextSteps.notice: I enjoyed the biology poster, but talking about patient care made me want to explore medicine. Keep design as an earlier interest.

nextSteps.title: Compare affordable design programs
nextSteps.detail: Compare curriculum, portfolio review, internships, software access, net price, and transfer credit. College can build skills and connections; employment still depends on demonstrated work.

nextSteps.title: Ask an employed designer about early-career work
nextSteps.detail: Ask about deadlines, client feedback, portfolio expectations, and full-time roles versus freelance hours and business expenses.

nextSteps.title: Explore a health question
nextSteps.detail: Use two reliable sources to explain a general health question. Notice whether you enjoy the science, explanation, or both. Use a public youth program for supervised exposure to healthcare.

nextSteps.title: Map college, medical school, and residency
nextSteps.detail: Compare college prerequisites, four-year medical training, and family medicine residency. Budget each stage separately; no college major guarantees medical school admission.

nextSteps.title: Ask about a normal day in family medicine
nextSteps.detail: Ask a physician and a resident about patient contact, documentation, training hours, and what they wish they knew in high school.
